Cd.binding_scope: Fats, oils, and fat emulsions (water-in-oil type)

iAs.label: Inorganic arsenic is a component of total arsenic (iAs <= tAs). The iAs value (100 ug/kg) is not below the binding total arsenic ceiling (100 ug/kg), so inorganic arsenic is governed by and bounded by the total arsenic ceiling; no separate iAs ceiling is published. The total arsenic is measured on every lot; on ongoing lots iAs is speciated whenever tAs exceeds its limit.

tHg.binding_scope: Fats, oils, and fat emulsions (water-in-oil type)

MeHg.label: Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). The MeHg value (20 ug/kg) is not below the binding total mercury ceiling (20 ug/kg), so methylmercury is governed by and bounded by the total mercury ceiling; no separate MeHg ceiling is published. The total mercury is measured on every lot; on ongoing lots MeHg is speciated whenever tHg exceeds its limit.

Ni.label: No government sets a nickel maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. This reads across the nearest applicable sovereign nickel ML on olive oil's own product-as-placed-on-market (liquid) basis: EU Reg 2024/1987 nickel in infant and young-child formula (liquid form), 100 ug/kg. The more permissive EU fruiting-vegetable nickel ML (400 ug/kg) was the alternative food-type sibling; it was rejected because it would admit oil at concentrations the primary literature flags as contaminated (ground-harvest samples reported at 220-330 ug/kg). Disclosed as a read-across, not direct EU governance of oil; clean commercial olive oil clears 100 ug/kg with headroom (Kabaran 2020 Cyprus n=27 mean 30, max 54; Llorent-Martinez 2014 virgin olive oil below detection).

Cr.source_scope: Raw milk, pasteurized milk, sterilized milk, modified milk and fermented milk (GB 2762-2025 Table 7, item 6.1); total Cr, not Cr-VI
Cr.label: No government sets a total-chromium maximum level for an edible oil or fat in any jurisdiction. This reads across the strictest real food total-chromium ML on the matching liquid, product-as-placed-on-market basis: China GB 2762-2022 total chromium in liquid milk, 300 ug/kg (test method GB 5009.123). Clean commercial olive oil passes (Kabaran 2020 Cyprus n=27 mean 124, max 218; Llorent-Martinez 2014 virgin olive oil below detection); grossly contaminated oil fails. This total-chromium ceiling is the reflex-speciation screen for the hexavalent-chromium control below. GB 2762-2025 supersedes GB 2762-2022 on 2026-09-02; re-verify this value against the 2025 revision at that time.

Cr-VI.label: No government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. This reads across the strictest drinking-water (oral-intake) Cr(VI) limit as a conservative species ceiling: the California State Water Resources Control Board Cr(VI) MCL, 10 ug/L (about 11 ug/kg at an oil density of 0.91, applied at 10 as slightly conservative). That MCL is a feasibility-set enforceable limit, not a health-based no-effect level (the California Public Health Goal is far lower); it is adopted only as the strictest real sovereign oral-intake Cr(VI) number. The value sits far below the total-chromium screen (300 ug/kg), so the species constraint holds. In a lipid food matrix hexavalent chromium reduces to trivalent chromium, so any total-chromium exceedance is reflex-speciated by IC-ICP-MS (EPA 3060A alkaline digestion + EPA 6800 / EN 15192) and any quantifiable Cr(VI) above 10 ug/kg fails.

Sn.source_scope: canned foods other than canned beverages, except canned dried and canned powdered products
Sn.label: No government sets a tin maximum level for an edible oil or fat. The only tin pathway in a bottled oil is migration from tin or tinplate packaging (Charfi 2026 measures 20 ug/kg from a tin container versus 120 ug/kg or below for glass and PET). This reads across the EU Reg 2023/915 inorganic-tin maximum level for canned foods other than beverages, 200000 ug/kg, on the identical product-as-placed-on-market basis: the sovereign instrument purpose-built to bound tin migrating from a metal contact surface into the food it holds. Real oil sits far below it; grossly tin-contaminated oil from failed packaging is caught.

Al.basis: specific migration into food; source unit mg/kg food
Al.label: No government sets an aluminium maximum level for an edible oil or fat. The demonstrated aluminium pathway in a bottled oil is migration from packaging (Charfi 2026: 670 ug/kg from aluminium containers versus 120 ug/kg or below for glass and PET). This reads across the EU Reg 10/2011 aluminium specific-migration limit, 1000 ug/kg, the sovereign instrument that bounds aluminium migrating into food from a contact material (derived against the EFSA aluminium tolerable weekly intake). The specific-migration limit is applied at face value as a conservative total-content ceiling; the elevated case arose from aluminium metal containers, and the migration limit is disclosed as the nearest sovereign anchor, not direct total-content governance of oil.

record.method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; face value, no reconstitution; read-across / control / not-material for unregulated cells; no occurrence percentiles)
record.lineage_note: Cat-30 government-limit standard, full-panel numeric completion (2026-08-25). Edible-oil MLs (EU 2023/915, Codex named-vegetable-oils, GSO 193:2021, Thailand MOPH 414, India FSSAI, Israel FCS) govern Pb/Cd/tAs/iAs/tHg at face value. The five previously-unregulated cells now carry adversarially-verified numeric read-across ceilings, each disclosed as a read-across to the nearest applicable sovereign instrument on the matching product-as-placed-on-market basis: Ni 100 (EU 2024/1987 formula-liquid), total-Cr 300 (China GB2762 liquid-milk), Cr-VI 10 (California SWRCB drinking-water MCL, conservative oral-intake species ceiling below the total-Cr screen), Sn 200000 (EU 2023/915 canned-food inorganic-tin, the packaging-migration pathway), Al 1000 (EU 10/2011 aluminium migration limit, the packaging-migration pathway). MeHg is bounded by the binding total-mercury ceiling (MeHg<=tHg by identity). Every panel analyte terminates in a testable ceiling; no null control/not-material cells remain (founder rule 2026-08-25).

record.name: Fermentation-derived / single-cell protein ingredients (precision-fermented, cultured, yeast-biomass proteins)
record.analog_label: the dried single-cell-protein / yeast-biomass fraction — read across from the strictest applicable dry plant-protein human-food analog (cereals, pulses, and legumes; adult/general human food, as sold)
record.feed_law_note: This subcategory covers a precision-fermented / single-cell / cultured PROTEIN INGREDIENT (spray-dried, heat-inactivated microbial biomass, e.g. Saccharomyces cerevisiae expressing an animal-identical protein) sold as a constituent of pet food. It is legally FEED (FDA CVM review, AAFCO, EU Directive 2002/32). Two read-across facts set the number honestly. First, a single-cell-protein biomass is not contamination-free by construction: anionic cell-wall groups biosorb Pb/Cd/Ni/Cr, arsenate is actively imported through the yeast phosphate transporters, and the metal load tracks the fermentation feedstock (plant sugars/molasses) and the mineral/trace-element premix — so Cd, Pb, and inorganic arsenic are real, load-bearing risks and are never marked not-material. Second, the strictest applicable HUMAN-FOOD analog on a dry as-sold basis is the plant-protein fraction (cereals, pulses, legumes), the same strict analog set the finished pet food already reads across; adopting it (rather than the looser same-class spec) keeps the ingredient limit at least as strict as any finished food it enters (Method v2.0 strictest-applicable rule, and the anti-circumvention guardrail against a looser ingredient tier laundering into a stricter finished food). The resulting toxic ceilings (Pb 20, Cd 40, tAs 100, iAs 100, tHg 20 ug/kg) are stricter on every toxic than the only governed same-class human-food spec, the EU novel-food Yarrowia lipolytica yeast-biomass Union-list contaminant limits (Pb 100, Cd 100, As 150, Hg 100 ug/kg; Reg (EU) 2019/760 amending 2017/2470), which is disclosed as the corroborating over-compliance floor and never selects the number. The applicable feed floor is disclosed on every row and never selects the number.
